pages.cta: Run a check of your shop

checks.title: What we check
checks.intro: We walk through your checkout, sign-up and cancellation flows like a customer would – and compare them with the rules.

items.title: The withdrawal button
items.body: Since 19 June 2026, customers who buy online must be able to withdraw through a clearly labelled function on the site, with a confirmation step and acknowledgement.

items.title: Misleading design
items.body: Fake urgency ("only 2 left"), pre-ticked add-ons, fees hidden until the last step and "no thanks" buttons that guilt-trip.

items.title: Subscriptions
items.body: How easy it is to cancel compared with signing up, and how free trials and renewals are communicated.

items.title: Digital Fairness Act
items.body: The European Commission proposed it on 11 November 2026. We show where you already differ from the proposed rules, so you can fix things calmly.

steps.title: Enter your address
steps.body: No installation and no login to your systems.

steps.title: We scan the flows
steps.body: Our agents click through the site and compare it with a rule library reviewed by lawyers.

steps.title: You get the report
steps.body: Screenshots, which rule applies, how serious it is and how to fix it.

compare.title: Free check or monitoring?
compare.intro: The free check shows where your shop stands today. Sites and rules change every week, so monitoring keeps you on the right side of them.

rows.label: Report with screenshots, rule and fix
Checkout and withdrawal flow
values: Every week, via a test account

rows.label: Alerts when something on the site breaks the rules
Alerts when the rules change, such as the Digital Fairness Act

items.a: No. {name} is an automated monitoring service. Our legal partner reviews the rule library, but the report does not replace advice on a specific case.

items.q: Do you need access to our systems?
items.a: No. We only look at what an ordinary customer sees on your site.

items.q: Can I request a check of someone else's website?
items.a: No. The free report is only sent to people who own or work for the website. We check this before sending.

items.q: Why do you ask for a test order?
items.a: The withdrawal button and its confirmation often only appear after a purchase. You get the report within 24 hours either way. If you place a test order and send us the order number, we check the whole flow and send an addendum within 24 hours.

items.q: What do you do in the checkout?
items.a: Only if you choose it when you request the check: we put an item in the cart and fill in {name}'s own company details up to payment, to see add-ons, the total price and the wording of the order button. We never press that button and never enter card details or anyone else's personal data. Without your permission we stop at the first step of the checkout.

items.q: What happens to my email address?
items.a: It is used for the report and one follow-up. Data is stored in the EU. You can ask us to delete it any time.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.draftNotice: Draft – to be reviewed by a lawyer before launch.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for your data
sections.body: The data controller is {company}, reg. no. {orgNr}, {address}.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: When you request a free check, we store the website you enter, your email address, the language you chose, whether you allowed us to go through the checkout, whether you plan to place a test order, and the time.

sections.heading: Why, and on what legal basis
sections.body: We use the data to produce and send the report and for one follow-up. The legal basis is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.

sections.heading: Where the data is stored and for how long
sections.body: The data is stored with our form provider inside the EU. We delete it no later than 12 months after the report is sent, or earlier if you ask us to.

sections.heading: Cookies and tracking
sections.body: This website uses no cookies and no advertising tracking.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access, correct and delete your data, and to complain to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY).
